title: Inverse: addition undoes subtraction
keyIdea: Addition and subtraction undo each other. You can check a sum by subtracting, and solve missing-number problems with the inverse.
familyTip: Write 13 + 5 = 18, then ask your child to say 18 − 5 = 13 without recounting. Next try □ + 9 = 14 using 14 − 9.

visual.caption: Inverse add and subtract — fair idea or myth? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: you must always recount from scratch

lab.caption: Flagship lab: undo an add, check a sum, solve a missing number, show a fact-family pair, reject recount-from-scratch, then challenge.

kid: Add and take away undo each other.
If 5 + 3 makes 8, then 8 − 3 brings you back to 5.
You can check a sum by subtracting. You can find a missing number the same way.
You do not need to count all over again from the start.
adult: NC Y2 / CCSS 1.OA.4: use the inverse link between addition and subtraction to check calculations and solve missing-number problems. Words: inverse, undo, check, missing number, fact family.
Common mistakes: thinking add and subtract are unrelated; recounting from scratch instead of reusing a fact; for □ + 9 = 14 adding 14 + 9 instead of subtracting.
In the lab your child undoes an add with subtract, checks 15 + 7 = 22 using 22 − 7, solves □ + 9 = 14, shows a fact-family pair, and rejects the recount myth.

practice.hint: Think of the reverse of adding the same number.
practice.explain: Subtract 3 undoes add 3, so you return to 5. That is what inverse means.

practice.hint: Use the reverse operation on the total to check the sum.
practice.explain: 22 − 7 = 15 checks that 15 + 7 = 22 using the same three numbers.

practice.explain: □ = {=a+b} − {b} = {a}. Missing-number problems use the undoing subtract.
